body:
SCOUT READ-ONLY TYPE-DISCIPLINE REVIEW of 7d3108d + 03c9564. Verdict: the same-view/recall law is correct and the empty-unit proof should remain accepted; 2 type-shape findings before I would call the public receipt/error surface finished. Chief ruling is authoritative; I made no edits and claimed no paths.

1. MAJOR, ADT stuffing at population.scala:274-290. PopulationAggregate reuses AlignError.FingerprintMismatch(field: String, recorded: String, derived: String), an error whose Scaladoc and message explicitly mean a fingerprint CARRIED ON THE WIRE. It stuffs subject identity into field strings such as "viewFingerprint (subject b)", and the tests then parse that string with startsWith/contains. This is a different failure: an in-memory population member proof does not match the aggregate view/recall. Recommendation: dedicated typed cases, e.g. PopulationViewMismatch(subject: SubjectId, proof: ViewFingerprint, aggregate: ViewFingerprint) and PopulationRecallMismatch(subject: SubjectId, proof: Checksum, suppliedRecall: Checksum). That preserves subject identity, keeps ViewFingerprint typed, and stops the message falsely saying "on the wire". It also answers the open FingerprintMismatch question: I recommend a dedicated ADT case, not the field-string reuse.

2. MAJOR, parallel receipt fields at population.scala:29-42. PopulationReceipt(viewFingerprint, subjectCount, recallChecksums, contentlessSubjects) is publicly constructible in inconsistent states, and sorting checksums independently destroys the subject-to-recall binding. The new contentlessSubjects vector adds a third parallel fact that can drift from the first two. Recommendation: a private/smart-constructed receipt containing a deterministic NonEmptyVector[PopulationMemberReceipt(subject, recallChecksum, unitPresence)], sorted by SubjectId; derive subjectCount, recallChecksums, and subjectsWithNoUnits from members. Library authors pay the proof burden; readers gain contributor-level provenance and impossible inconsistent counts.

VISION WORDING: the observable predicate is recall.units.isEmpty. That does NOT by itself prove the participant was silent or "recalled nothing"; it can also mean no units were segmented/resolved. Keep accepting it, but name it subjectsWithNoRecallUnits / NoUnits and reserve "silent participant" for evidence that actually establishes silence. The test itself uses non-empty source text ("nothing here.") with zero units, demonstrating why the distinction matters.

PLAN RECONCILIATION: upheld—same-view identity, per-recall binding, sparse aggregation, legitimate absence, and Discipline laws. Silently weakened—typed AlignError semantics and a self-consistent contributor receipt. ERGONOMICS: adding RecallGraph to SubjectAlignment is a meaningful identity choice, not proof bookkeeping; no convenience default hides it. SHOULD-HAVE-CHANGED: AlignError needed the new population cases; PopulationReceipt needed a member type. No suppressions, casts, widened Any/String maps, unlawful instances, or production throws found. Verified from the exact two-commit diff and all construction/match sites; test green is author evidence, not rerun by me.
